items.followUp: State two roles of apoptosis in the body.

rubric.why: Apoptosis removes damaged, unwanted or extra cells.
rubric.description: States that apoptosis removes or destroys cells that are damaged or no longer needed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the removal or destruction of damaged, unwanted or extra cells.

rubric.why: Apoptosis helps shape body parts during normal development.
rubric.description: Gives a developmental role of apoptosis, such as separating developing fingers and toes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid developmental role, such as shaping body parts or separating developing fingers and toes.

modelAnswer: Apoptosis removes damaged, unwanted or extra cells from the body.
It helps in the normal development and shaping of body parts, for example, by separating developing fingers and toes.

items.followUp: Where does glycolysis occur, and what is its main product?

rubric.why: Glycolysis is the breakdown or splitting of glucose.
rubric.description: Identifies glucose as the molecule broken down in glycolysis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glycolysis breaks down or splits glucose.

rubric.why: Glycolysis produces two molecules of pyruvic acid and takes place in the cytoplasm.
rubric.description: Gives the product or location of glycolysis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glycolysis produces two molecules of pyruvic acid or occurs in the cytoplasm.

modelAnswer: Glycolysis is the breakdown of one glucose molecule into two molecules of pyruvic acid.
It takes place in the cytoplasm of the cell.
